## Problem 1

b. From Problem1_2_start.R:

Annotation to the code was improved and adjusted

```{r}
library(deSolve)
library(ggplot2)


TI.model <- function(t, x, parms) {
  Ta <- x[1] # pop 1
  I  <- x[2] # pop 2
  with(as.list(parms),{
    dT <- lambda- deltaT * Ta - beta * Ta * I #changes in pops
    dI <- beta * Ta * I - deltaI * I #changes in pop
    res <- c(dT, dI)
    list(res)
  })
}

### by varying beta 
parmsTI  <- c(lambda = 1000, 
               deltaT = 0.05,
               deltaI = log(2)/1.39,
               beta = NA)
parmsTI["beta"] <- 5/(parmsTI["lambda"]/parmsTI["deltaT"]/parmsTI["deltaI"]) #why 5 / rest?
xstartTI <- c(Ta = as.numeric(parmsTI["lambda"]/parmsTI["deltaT"]), 
               I = 1) #why divide by death percent??
times  <- seq(0, 100, length=500)

#here rk4 is a function provided by R to solve differential equations which you do not have to understand in further detail
out.TI <- as.data.frame(rk4(xstartTI, times, TI.model, parmsTI))

out.TI_long = out.TI |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols= -time) 

#plotting of the numerically solved quantities
#fill in the gaps by yourself
ggplot(data =  out.TI_long, mapping= aes(x = time, y = value, color = name)) +
  geom_line(lwd = 1) +
  theme_classic() 

```














Problem 2 - Exercise c 

Calculate the parameters for rate I

```{r}
#import data
virusLoad <- read_csv("Content_per_day/Day_two_content/Exercises Olat Upload/data/virusLoadOnTreatment.csv")

ggplot(virusLoad, aes(x = time, y = V)) +
  geom_point()



getSSG <- function(parm){
  Io_fi <- parm[1]
  deltaI <- parm[2]
  
  I_fit <- Io_fi * exp((-deltaI) * virusLoad$time)
  SSQ <- (log(I_fit) - log(virusLoad$V))**2
  
  return(sum(SSQ))

}

I0_fit <- optim(par = c(1, 1), fn = getSSG)$par[1]
deltaI_fit <- optim(par = c(1,1), fn = getSSG)$par[2]



ggplot(virusLoad, aes(x = time, y = log(V))) +
  geom_point()

model <- lm(log(V) ~ time, virusLoad)
deltaI_est <- summary(model)["coefficients"][[1]][1]


#calculate t1/2



#t1/2 
t1_2 <- log(1/2)/(deltaI_fit)

```
